name: Eurostat dissemination API
publisher: Eurostat (Statistical Office of the European Union)
description: The EU's official statistics, harmonised across member states so that the numbers are actually comparable -- GDP and national accounts, population and migration, labour, prices, energy, trade, health and regional breakdowns down to NUTS level 3. About 8,000 datasets, each addressed by a short code (nama_10_gdp, demo_pjan, prc_hicp_midx), queryable keyless as JSON-stat, and with the full SDMX structure available if you need the dimension definitions.
geography: EU member states, EFTA, candidate countries; many series down to NUTS 2 and NUTS 3 regions

temporal.start: 1960 for national accounts; most series start 1990-2000
temporal.grain: annual, quarterly and monthly depending on the dataset
temporal.updated: per release calendar; the response carries an `updated` timestamp

license.name: Commission Reuse Decision 2011/833/EU -- free reuse with attribution
license.redistribution: permitted, including commercially, with the source acknowledged

access.size_hint: a filtered query is a few KB; a whole dataset as TSV runs to tens of MB
access.rate_limit: 50 requests per 10 seconds per IP (documented); a single query is also capped at 1,000,000 cells
access.pagination: none -- you narrow with dimension filters instead, and a query that would exceed the cell cap is rejected rather than truncated
access.etiquette: filter on the server with geo/time/unit parameters rather than pulling a whole dataset and subsetting locally

probes.description: One cell of German GDP, current prices
The dataset index, with last-update dates
probes.note: About 3 MB in full. range_bytes stops the read at the header rows, which is all the probe needs.

recipes.title: One indicator for every member state, one year
Find the dataset code for a subject
JSON-stat is a flat array plus index maps, not nested records
recipes.code:
import json, urllib.request
u = ('https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/'
     'nama_10_gdp?format=JSON&na_item=B1GQ&unit=CP_MEUR&time=2023')
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(u))
geo = d['dimension']['geo']['category']
label, index = geo['label'], geo['index']
# `value` is keyed by flat position as a string, and missing cells are simply absent
for code, pos in sorted(index.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]):
    v = d['value'].get(str(pos))
    if v is not None:
        print('%-28s %12.0f' % (label[code], v))

gotchas.trap: JSON-stat does not return records. `value` is a flat map from a stringified integer position to a number, and you have to reconstruct the coordinates yourself from `dimension`, `id` and `size`.
gotchas.fix: Read `id` for dimension order and `size` for the shape, then decode each position as a row-major index. For a single-dimension query the position is just the value of `dimension.<name>.category.index[code]`, which is what the Python recipe above uses.

gotchas.trap: Missing observations are absent from `value`, not null. Iterating over value.items() silently skips countries rather than reporting them as missing.
gotchas.fix: Iterate over the dimension's index and look each position up with .get(), so an absent cell shows as missing rather than vanishing from the output.

gotchas.trap: A query that would return more than a million cells is rejected outright rather than truncated, and it is easy to write one by accident -- omitting `time` on a monthly regional dataset will do it.
gotchas.fix: Always pin at least one of geo, time or unit. If you genuinely want everything, take the bulk TSV instead of paging the API.

gotchas.trap: Dataset codes look mnemonic but are not guessable, and old codes are retired without redirects.
gotchas.fix: Resolve the code from the catalogue TOC rather than hard-coding one you found in a paper. The TOC also carries `last update of data`, which is how you tell a discontinued series from a slow one.

gotchas.trap: `geo` codes are mostly ISO-3166 alpha-2 but not entirely: EL is Greece, not GR, and UK is the United Kingdom, not GB. EU27_2020 and EA19/EA20 are aggregates that will double-count if you sum the column.
gotchas.fix: Map EL->GR and UK->GB when joining to anything ISO, and drop codes matching EU*, EA* and *_AGG before aggregating.

gotchas.trap: Values carry status flags (p provisional, e estimated, b break in series, c confidential) in a parallel `status` object that most clients drop.
gotchas.fix: Read `status` before drawing a trend line across a `b`. A break in series means the definition changed, not that the quantity did.

fields: geo -- country or NUTS region code; EL and UK are the exceptions to ISO
time -- year, or 2024-Q1 / 2024-01 forms depending on the dataset's frequency
unit -- CP_MEUR (current prices), CLV_I10 (chain-linked volume index), PC (percent); comparing across units is a common error
na_item -- the national-accounts concept, e.g. B1GQ for GDP
freq -- A, Q or M; present as a dimension even when the dataset has only one value for it
status -- provisional/estimated/break flags, in a parallel object to value
